timing.question: Why do the two dashboards show different totals?

approach.quote: I will actually give them both more ACUs in their tiers

next_step.quote: I would have to ask support

tag_question_examples: it is actually all there, isn't it?

must_mention.point: Organization limit and per-user tier are enforced independently; either one blocks, and raising one never lifts the other
The Trailhead lead is at 180 of 400 on her tier but Trailhead is at 3,000 of 3,000, so only an enterprise admin raising the org limit helps
The per-user meter counts cloud plus local usage and leaves Devin Review out; the org limit includes Review
must_mention.evidence_quote: at 410, cloud plus local, and his Review usage is not counted

must_mention.point: Limits reset on the contract day, the 23rd, after the 18–20 Nov sale, and temporary overrides expire then
Newest vs Legacy is the gear-icon Version setting; Cloud-only metrics exclude local usage; the empty state means no billing cycle in range
A tier applies to each member, not a pooled team budget; a team cap is an organization-level limit
The finance update carried exactly three ACU figures, each with the view it came from

repeated_words: "I think" ×2 in place of a number
clarification_requests: "which is the total" — coach: which dashboard is that from?
article_plural_slips: "more ACUs in their tiers" — tiers are not per person budgets to top up; "a higher limit"
sentences_to_rerecord: Basically the Trailhead lead has a tier and she ran out, I think, and the Lumen person also ran out.

accuracy.anchor: One of seven points (mm3); the Trailhead block misread as a tier problem (anchor: 0–8 = mechanism wrong).

structure.anchor: No outcome sentence and no evidence step; the update was two sentences (anchor: 0–8 = no discernible order).

customer_relevance.anchor: No figure for finance; "the numbers are on the dashboard" (anchor: 0–7 = talks about pages, not impact).

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Framing 40 s over, every other segment far under; nine fillers, one tag question, two long pauses (anchor: 0–5 = most segments off, fillers above 1/min).

recovery.anchor: Both objections answered by assertion or deferral (anchor: 0–3 = no acknowledgement, no evidence).

"She was under her own cap; the organization was not." — check which meter is full before proposing a fix.
"That's fair. The boundary is … The evidence is … I can offer …" — use it for both objections.
